The common thread

Read the mechanism ↗
  • Fixed issuance: 1B BULLEN originally; mint and freeze authority revoked.
  • Collecting: paid claims commit tokens for later destruction.
  • Market activity: eligible trades produce creator fees.
  • Distinct effects: burns outside the pool do not change its reserve-ratio spot price.

Completing the reserved routes would leave about 452.35M BULLEN. The further 352.35M is a planning ceiling, not an allocation exclusively available to the platform. Supply discipline needs execution discipline. Reserve capacity for accepted claims first, reconcile every managed route before execution and stop new discretionary burns at the boundary. Independent holders can still burn their own tokens. A global floor is not enforced by the existing programs.

04 / A new source of fuel

Revenue with
a return route.

The proposed platform policy connects a new business to the House. Product income funds continued development and a defined contribution to BULLEN.

Proposed platform policy

Earn. Reinvest.
Repeat.

Platform monetization includes transaction fees and paid product offerings, where the relevant payment routes are enabled. Only realized, reconciled net funds this proposal.

THE BASE: DISTRIBUTABLE NET

Cash remaining after operating costs, payment and network costs, refunds, taxes and existing obligations. Gross transaction volume is not revenue. A listed plan is not a collected payment.

No assumed revenue, token price or completion date is used in the supply accounting.

25%

Market buybacks & burns

Buy BULLEN with allocated net proceeds, then destroy the acquired tokens within the shared supply allowance.

25%

Declared marketing allocation

Outreach, distribution and growth. Actual spend remains need-led; additional reinvestment can support it.

50%

Remaining reinvestment capacity

Product, operations, reserves and—if adopted—liquidity. A flexible budget, not a fixed personal payout.

The game has its own allocations.

Card preorders allocate 20% to BULLEN buyback/burn. Eligible original crypto editions allocate $7.50 / $15 / $25 at their $25 / $50 / $100 prices. Direct support allocates 10% of eligible receipts excluding tax, before payment fees; historical payment terms remain attached to their orders. The remaining funding supports production. A game-funded HERD giveaway uses an existing mint slot and its burn; that burn is not counted again as an additional game route.

Funding & allocation terms ↗

Creator fees keep the House moving.

Eligible referrals receive 50% of measured creator fees on qualifying buys. The Drop uses 25% of qualifying buy creator fees. Ten designated NFTs share 20% after the marketing allocation; published marketing-backer participation is up to 25%. These use different bases and eligibility rules, so they are not one additive percentage split. Requested secondary NFT royalties are separate again; they are not guaranteed receipts.

01 / FUND

Use reinvestment funds.

Trial a liquidity budget from the discretionary remainder after the 25% burn and 25% marketing allocations. Keep an operating reserve. No permanent LP percentage is assumed.

02 / PAIR

Verify the venue.

PumpSwap lists a deposit restriction for boost pools. Resolve that compatibility first; a new full-range Raydium CPMM pool is a candidate if existing-pool deposits are unavailable.

03 / LIMIT

Pair new capital.

Acquire both assets using fresh quotes and impact limits. Keep burn reserves and mint escrow untouched. Connect any new venue to fee, referral, giveaway and volume accounting before treating it as equivalent.

04 / REVIEW

Measure before expanding.

Compare routing and trade-size impact before expanding. Publish LP custody and lock terms. New positions are withdrawable unless explicitly locked; fees do not eliminate impermanent loss.

The recommendation: earmark a measured liquidity budget from available reinvestment, then release it only to a verified, integrated venue. A separate full-range pool may be the practical route; concentrated liquidity adds active range management. Treat 100M as a conditional managed-burn boundary, with a separately adopted policy for unspent future burn allocations.

The current PumpSwap interface explicitly lists deposits/withdrawals as unsupported for boost pools. This pool has nonzero virtual reserves, so this plan does not promise a native top-up. A separate pool can split liquidity and creator-fee income; integration and routing tests are prerequisites. Liquidity tokens represent ownership, not destroyed BULLEN.

The pool currently contains slightly more than the proposed entire final supply. Future buys can change that balance, so it is not a permanent contradiction. It does mean the floor cannot be reached while pool and holder balances stay unchanged. Never remove liquidity simply to burn its token side.

What this proposal does—and does not—commit to

The 25% platform buyback/burn allocation, 25% declared platform marketing allocation, 100M stopping rule and additional liquidity program are proposals. Existing mint, preorder, referral, creator-fee and custody terms continue to govern their own routes. This page does not change those terms or authorize any transaction.

The snapshot’s total supply is 818,148,430.922664 BULLEN; finalized destruction is 181,851,569.077336. Shared variable-route capacity is 352,348,430.922664 after reserving 237.5M for the remaining volume schedule, 111M for the remaining HERD, 17.3M for available paid Object claims and 100M to remain. Remaining available stock is reserved at the maximum paid-claim case; awards may reduce that maximum. Amounts are from separate reads within the stated audit window, not an atomic multi-program transaction.

A floor requires coordinated claim admission, reserved capacity and burn execution checks. It cannot stop independent token owners from burning. Liquidity provision requires capital, carries impermanent-loss and custody risk, and does not create guaranteed price support. At the floor, committed obligations and the policy for unspent allocations must be resolved before new managed burns or claims are accepted.

Current supply may be fetched separately when this page runs on the House website. The full commitment ledger remains the dated audited snapshot until a new reconciliation is published; a fresh supply number alone is not enough to recompute it safely.
